questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design immutable audit and backup pipelines across multi-account and multi-region SAP deployments, ensuring regulatory retention, tamper-evidence, and auditable disaster recovery tests.

## Key Concepts
- S3 Object Lock in Governance mode for SAP HANA backups
- Cross-region replication for DR bucket redundancy
- CloudTrail multi-region trails combined with OpenTelemetry exporting to a central data lake
- Cross-account KMS CMK grants with key rotation implications
- Least-privilege IAM roles and Service Control Policies (SCPs)
- DR validation and audit integrity verification procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  SapBackupsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub 'sap-backups-${AWS::AccountId}'
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      ObjectLockEnabled: true
      ObjectLockDefaultRetention:
        Mode: GOVERNANCE
        Days: 365
      BucketPolicy:
        PolicyText:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:
            - Sid: DenyDeleteWithGovernance
              Effect: Deny
              Principal: '*'
              Action: 's3:DeleteObject'
              Resource:
                - !Sub '${SapBackupsBucket.Arn}/*'
              Condition:
                StringNotEquals:
                  s3:SignatureAge: '3600000'
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical ABAC integration between SAP HANA on EC2 and AWS IAM across multiple accounts, plus real-world testing and auditing.

## Key Concepts
- ABAC sourcing (SSO attributes, tags, principal tags)
- Cross-account trust and policy generation
- SAP authorization propagation and auditing

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  SAPABACRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: 2012-10-17
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: '*'
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:PrincipalTag/SAPEnvironment: Prod
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: SAPReadWriteProd
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: 2012-10-17
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: [ 's3:GetObject', 's3:PutObject' ]
                Resource: 'arn:aws:s3:::sap-prod-data/*'
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests a practical end-to-end patching flow, including OS and SAP layers, sandbox testing, rollback, and monitoring.

## Key Concepts
- AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
- SAP SUM patching workflow
- IAM roles, least privilege
- Snapshots/AMI rollback
- CloudWatch compliance

## Code Example
```yaml
# CloudFormation snippet for patch role and baseline
Resources:
  PatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: [ec2.amazonaws.com, ssm.amazonaws.com]
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      Path: '/'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PatchManagerPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'ec2:DescribeInstances'
                  - 'ssm:SendCommand'
                  - 'ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation'
                Resource: '*'
  SAPPatchBaseline:
    Type: AWS::SSM::PatchBaseline
    Properties:
      Name: SAP-OS-Patch-Baseline
      OperatingSystem: AMAZON_LINUX_2
      ApprovalRules:
        PatchRules:
          - PatchFilterGroup:
              PatchFilters:
                - PatchFilter:
                    Key: CLASSIFICATION
                    Type: EQUAL
                    Values: ['Security','Critical']
            AutoApprove: true
            ComplianceLevel: 100
```

- How would you verify SAP patch success end-to-end

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of fundamental AWS networking for SAP: private isolation, controlled admin access, and audit-friendly egress.

## Key Concepts
- VPC design with private subnets for SAP components
- Bastion host as controlled admin access point
- NAT gateway for outbound updates
- Security groups enforcing least privilege on SAP ports
- Basic cost- and log-awareness with flow logs

## Code Example
```terraform
# Minimal Terraform example for core resources
provider "aws" { region = "us-east-1" }

# VPC
resource "aws_vpc" "sap_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"
  enable_dns_support = true
  enable_dns_hostnames = true
}

# Subnets
resource "aws_subnet" "private_a" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.1.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1a"
}
resource "aws_subnet" "private_b" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.2.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1b"
}
resource "aws_subnet" "public_bastion" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.0.3.0/24"
  availability_zone = "us-east-1a"
  map_public_ip_on_launch = true
}

# Internet & NAT
resource "aws_internet_gateway" "igw" { vpc_id = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id }
resource "aws_nat_gateway" "nat" {
  allocation_id = aws_eip.nat.id
  subnet_id     = aws_subnet.public_bastion.id
}
resource "aws_eip" "nat" { vpc = true }

# Security Groups
resource "aws_security_group" "sap_sg" {
  name        = "sap_sg"
  description = "SAP ports restricted"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
}
resource "aws_security_group" "bastion_sg" {
  name        = "bastion_sg"
  description = "Bastion host access"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.sap_vpc.id
}

# Ingress rules
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "sap_ingress" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 30015
  to_port           = 30019
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.sap_sg.id
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
}
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "sap_ingress2" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 3200
  to_port           = 3205
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.sap_sg.id
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
}
# SSH access to Bastion only from corporate IPs
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "bastion_ssh" {
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 22
  to_port           = 22
  protocol          = "tcp"
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion_sg.id
  cidr_blocks       = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: IAM Role and CloudWatch Alarm for SAP HANA EC2
Resources:
  SAPCloudWatchRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: ec2.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: S3LogArchival
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: arn:aws:logs:*:*:*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:PutObject
                Resource: arn:aws:s3:::sap-logs-archive/*
  CPUAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: sap-hana-cpu-high
      AlarmDescription: Alert when CPU exceeds 80%
      MetricName: CPUUtilization
      Namespace: AWS/EC2
      Statistic: Average
      Period: 300
      EvaluationPeriods: 2
      Threshold: 80
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      Dimensions:
        - Name: InstanceId
          Value: !Ref SAP HANALinux
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref SNSTopic
```
